input: nums1 and nums2 are lists of m and n integers respectively, with 0 <= m,n <= 500 and values in [1,2000]. Empty lists are explicit extensions. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The maximum number of noncrossing connections between equal values in the two lists, using each index at most once. Equivalently, return the longest common subsequence length. The input lists need not be sorted and repeated values are allowed.
mutation_aliasing: Both caller lists and all entries remain unchanged, including when the same container is supplied twice. A private DP row is updated in place while a scalar retains the overwritten previous diagonal. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Every DP cell and diagonal is an integer in [0,min(m,n)], at most 500. An equal-value transition increments a valid prior-prefix count by one and remains within that bound. All index and recurrence arithmetic are exact safe integers.
complexity: O(m*(n+1)+n+1) time including row initialization and empty-inner-loop outer iterations, and O(n+1) auxiliary space. Only one row and its previous diagonal are retained; no full DP table, reconstruction or input copy is hidden.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 478 UTF-8 bytes, including all 0 declared helper definitions/statements and their calls, wrappers, closure/state definitions, built-in operations, allocations, annotations/comments where present, whitespace and terminal newline.
